findings.subject: Moon Pyramid obsidian workshop — Deposit 1
findings.place: Front J Pit 2, northwest of Moon Pyramid, Teotihuacan
findings.period: Xolalpan-associated deposition; direct absolute date unavailable
findings.assertion: In 2002, Carballo excavated 1.253 m³ of Deposit 1 within a shallow depression in tepetate, retrieving 170.6 kg of screened obsidian debitage (136.16 kg/m³). The feature reached 42 cm below surface and was estimated to be one-third of the surviving truncated deposit.
findings.evidence_type: excavated lithic refuse, field volume and mass measurement
findings.source_material_inspected: Publisher-hosted full PDF's text extraction for pp.53–55; figures' captions read, images not visually verified
findings.confidence: high for excavated sample; estimated fraction/truncation uncertain
findings.limitations: Depositional context may be dumped refuse rather than in situ floor; modern road and bulldozing altered feature

findings.subject: Ceramic chronology of Deposit 1
findings.period: Teotihuacan ceramic phases; later intrusive materials
findings.assertion: Table 3.1 assigns 534 small pottery fragments from Deposit 1: Miccaotli 168, Tlamimilolpa 173, Xolalpan 157, Tzacualli 27, Patlachique 3, Coyotlatelco 7, Aztec 1. Excavators used paste-based identification for heavily eroded sherds; the Xolalpan association is contextual, not a radiocarbon date.
findings.evidence_type: ceramic phase tabulation from excavation units 9, 9ex and 11
findings.source_material_inspected: Original table text extracted from publisher-hosted PDF
findings.confidence: high for reported tabulation, lower for deposit's exact depositional date
findings.limitations: No carbon or clean direct dating; contaminated by modern roadworks, sherds redeposited and eroded; tabulated category totals may not sum exactly as reported, requires checking original printed table image

findings.subject: Contrasting lithic assemblages west of Moon Pyramid
findings.place: Deposits 1–3 west and northwest of Moon Pyramid
findings.assertion: In the analyzed subsets Carballo counted 31,690 lithics (18.86 kg) in Deposit 1, 5,542 (3.51 kg) in Deposit 2, and 2,859 (7.86 kg) in Deposit 3. Average artifact masses were 0.60, 0.63 and 2.75 g respectively; the larger fragments in Deposit 3 reflect a different reduction regime.
findings.limitations: Analyzed sample is not the entire recovered assemblage; Deposit 2 includes grab samples with selection biases

findings.subject: Moon Pyramid obsidian supply composition and sampling bias
findings.assertion: In Table 5.1 Deposit 3 is visually classified as 45% gray, 53% green and 2% mahogany obsidian, including 22% of the total provisionally attributable to Tulancingo. Carballo explicitly contrasts the 22% visual figure with roughly 50% Tulancingo in a nonrandom geochemical subset, rejecting the subset as representative of the deposit.
findings.locator: Carballo 2011 pp.85–86, Table 5.1 and Appendix A discussion
findings.evidence_type: visual lithic raw material classification with selective LA-ICP-MS comparison
findings.source_material_inspected: Original table and explanatory passage read in publisher PDF text layer; Appendix A original full tables not inspected
findings.confidence: high for reported raw material classifications; provenance percentage provisional
findings.limitations: visual geologic sourcing not definitive; geochemical sampling expressly nonrandom and not population representative

findings.subject: Estimated dart point output from Deposit 1
findings.place: Front J Pit 2 northwest of Moon Pyramid
findings.assertion: Carballo compares four methods for extrapolating dart-point production from Deposit 1's lithic waste. The modeled estimates span 1,836–11,760 points, with a mean of 4,358; removing the model with a 3.4% assumed preform-breakage rate yields mean 3,242. These are modeled possible output quantities, not directly observed projectile counts.
findings.evidence_type: experimental-archaeology production models calibrated to excavated debitage
findings.source_material_inspected: Table 5.7 and methodological passage via PDF text layer
findings.confidence: moderate for documented model, low for true historical production count
findings.limitations: Multipliers for surviving deposit (3x) and bulldozed loss (2x) plus experimental error rates dominate ranges; model results should not be passed as measured output
